elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: 8.2 retains automatic renewal ("Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives sixty (60) days' advance written notice"), and not every conditional automatic-renewal element is satisfied: the opt-out window is 60 days (not \u226430) and no Vendor renewal reminder exists. To meet this element the drafter must either convert 8.2 to renewal only by mutual written agreement, or repair the 30-day opt-out and 60-day reminder limbs.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: 8.2 as rendered: "Each Order Form renews for twelve months" \u2014 a 12-month renewal term, no multi-year rollover.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered 8.2 requires "sixty (60) days' advance written notice"; the preferred ceiling is 30 days. Repair by setting the Customer non-renewal notice period to thirty (30) days.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No renewal-reminder obligation appears anywhere in 8.2 or 8.3; 8.3's ninety-day notice relates only to a Fee increase, not to the fact of renewal. Repair by inserting an express Vendor obligation to notify Customer at least 60 days before each renewal date.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: 8.3 (unchanged): "Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent."

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Rendered 8.2 sets the window at "sixty (60) days' advance written notice" for either Party, so Customer's non-renewal window is exactly 60 days, at the fallback ceiling; deterministic check "non-renewal notice window \u2264 60 days" returned ok.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: 8.3 caps each renewal uplift at "the lesser of" CPI and "three percent", which is necessarily \u22645 percent; already met without amendment.

reasons: Fallback is complete: the single edit converts the 180-day window in 8.2 to sixty (60) days (\u226460-day ceiling), and the retained 8.3 CPI/3% cap already satisfies the \u22645% pricing limb.

Preferred is not complete: the opt-out remains at 60 days rather than 30, and no Vendor renewal reminder (\u226560 days before renewal) exists in operative language; the margin comment acknowledges these are unpressed, and a promise in a comment does not count.

Minimal: the only textual change is the numeric notice period in 8.2 \u2014 renewal term length, the mutual "either Party" structure, and all of 8.3 (CPI/3% cap, ninety-day increase notice, prepaid-period carve-out) are retained unchanged; no survival tails, procedures, or out-of-checklist requirements added.

Preserves intent: no undefined terms, dangling cross-references, or contradictory retained sentences; the twelve-month term, Fee-increase notice mechanic, and prepaid protection continue to operate coherently with the shortened window.
Finding status "deviation" is correct: the original 180-day window exceeded the 90-day walk-away threshold, so a redline was warranted rather than a rationale note.
